doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
title: Will the big bands come back
summary: Pete says big bands cost too much to keep; Vegas and rock venues are the main outlets; Ellington carries on.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Go ahead, please. You're on the air.
I was wondering if you think the big bands will ever come back. And I have another question. I'd like to know what instrument Eddie Miller plays, and I'll hang up and listen to it.
I should have mentioned that. I thought everybody knew. Tenor saxophone.
Okay. How about the big bands, gents? Eddie, you worked with some.

Well, I think I'd like to see them come back. I really would, but... I think it's on the way. You think they really ever went? Well, I mean, to keep a band intact now, with the cost of keeping a band up of any size. It's a salary that you have to pay. And you can't find many places that will pay the money. Vegas is making us, I think, making a big effort to bring back. Right, they're the only Buddy Rich, you know, has... Big bands. There's a lot of big bands. But that's the only place they can work. They can work three months or a year there. And then after that, they just have to do some money.

Buddy's band has been working some of the rock places, though, like Fillmore East and Fillmore West. And the kids are dancing to big bands. Don Ellis, Blood, Sweat, and Tears is a reasonably big band.
That's right. Look, about... Say, my band is up to nine to ten pieces. But it's pretty big.
But Ellington's never gone out of business. No.
